From: Amanda Fagerblom <[contact omitted]>
Date: Mon, 22 Aug 2022 at 11:35
Subject: Fwd: FYSA FOLLOW UP: META/FB Points of Contact and Trainings
To: Nora Pinzon <[contact omitted]>, Daniel Dedeyan <[contact omitted]>
CC: Cara Thanassi <[contact omitted]>, Carrie Mitchell <[contact omitted]>
Hello Nora and Danny - Following up on the USAID LAC conversation with Meta/FB, please see Cara's email below and
the attachment from Meta/FB. A phone call with Mission leadership, LAC bureau, and Meta/FB would be helpful given the
sensitivities and security concerns around programming in country. The notes below are for us/USAID (but comfortable
sharing to Meta/FB by phone)
I think continued engagement would be useful. Here is some initial thinking:
General points:
• Who is the Meta/FB POC for Nicaragua?
• What are the ongoing, FB-funded initiatives/support in Nicaragua (or regional that include Nicaragua)? I had
heard there was something around connectivity along the border with Honduras (regional) when I was with
Internews. This would be helpful to know so we can ensure our radio/media partners are aware of potential
• Stressing the point: the information space is radilly closing with very few on the ground professional reporters.
In-country media and digital literacy is incredibly low despite high mobile penetration rates, leaving many
Nicaraguans -in particular those new to the online world- susceptible to misinformation.
• Given the significant number of Nicaraguans forced into exile in Costa Rica, Mission stresses the importance
for Meta/FB to incorporate strategies for Costa Rica to include Nicaraguan diaspora.
• Costa Rica-Nicaragua Initiatives: Many of our Nicaraguan media, business, and civil society partners are
operating bi-nationally, legally registered in Costa Rica, but with main audiences and content in and related to
• Mission is looking at medium-term planning and worst-case scenarios that include internet disruptions and
blocking, coordinated account takedowns of independent media, small enterprises, and civil society social media
accounts, among others. The overarching concern for us is the timeline. Space is closing rapidly and
increasingly looking like a Cuba scenario.
Areas I see helpful collaboration for Nicaragua under Meta/FB lines of Central America support:
1. Elections and Integrity Efforts: Investigations and Account Removals. Despite the Municipal elections in
November 2022 being called already with opposition in jail and forced exile, we anticipate the regime to silence
independent voices in social media and carry out coordinated misinformation campaigns and coordinated
account takedown attacks via troll networks. Investigations into the coordination (potentially increased over
elections) may help us better understand the real risk and increased capacities of adversaries online so we can
better adapt our digital security training and online safety for Nicaraguan partners. The quarterly adversarial threat
report and coordinated inauthentic behavior report have been useful. With regard to the OAS cooperation
agreement Meta/FB signed with the OAS, we want to know how our partners can plug into that.
2. Circulating phishing campaigns targeting Nicaraguans in WhatsApp: Our Nicaraguan partners and digital
